signals.text: Revenue grew 17% a year over 3 years vs 23% over 5: growth is slowing.
Profit compounded at 8% vs revenue at 17%: profits are lagging sales.
Operating margin compressed 95 bps in 3 years (8.5% → 7.5%).
Over 5 years, operating cash flow was 105% of reported profit: profits are turning into cash.
Free cash flow was negative in 3 of the last 5 years: capex is running ahead of cash generation.

guidance.statement: We will need some capex as we want to pursue increasing store count.
guidance.quote: If you see last year, capex was upwards of INR4,000 crores, and with the increasing store count that we want to pursue, we will need some capex - that is the plan.

guidance.statement: We might go to an INR2,000 crores borrowing by the end of the year, going towards managing capex.
guidance.quote: So we might go to an INR2,000 crores borrowing by the end of the year, but that is all going towards managing capex.

guidance.statement: Internally, our benchmarks will remain opening around 15% of our store base annually.
guidance.quote: So I do want to state that internally, our benchmarks will remain that we should be opening around 15% of our store base as the number that we want to increase annually.

delivered.statement: Reported a turnover of close to INR67,000 crores in the year gone by.
EBITDA margin came in at about 7.8% for the year.
Profit after tax was about 4.8%, reaching INR3,224 crores.
Like-for-like store growth for stores more than two years old grew about 8.1%.
Retail business area reached about 20.6 million square feet at the end of March 2026.
Total store count crossed the 500-store milestone last year.

calls.tone: confident on long-term physical retail model, cautious on e-commerce losses, and disciplined on expansion

pushback.gist: Analysts repeatedly questioned the long-term impact and sustainability of DMart's model against aggressive quick commerce expansion and pricing parity.
Pressed on slowing SSSG in mature metro stores and whether low single-digit growth is the new normal.
Challenged on why store additions remain capped at 15% despite ample capital, unconstrained manpower, and openness to leasing.
Questioned why AEL EBITDA losses and costs remain high despite right-sizing and exiting cities.

business.summary: Avenue Supermarts operates retail stores under the DMart brand, providing everyday low prices through everyday low-cost operations, alongside an e-commerce grocery delivery service called DMart Ready.

delivered.statement: Added 85 stores in FY 2025-26, ending the year with 500 stores.

calls.tone: Satisfactory performance across key operational and financial parameters, with a steady focus on EDLC/EDLP value retailing and cluster expansion.
